exam.title: Numerical Mathematics I - Exam B
exam.subtitle: Iterative methods, interpolation, integration, least squares
exam.instructions: Complete all tasks thoroughly. Provide algorithms explicitly and perform error estimates. Permitted aids: non-programmable calculator.

exercises.title: Jacobi method
exercises.description:
Given $4x - y = 3$, $-x + 4y = 3$ (exact solution $(1,1)$).
a) Carry out two steps of the Jacobi method with $\vec x^{(0)} = (0,0)$.
b) Justify convergence and give the convergence rate.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Iteration rule
Solving the $i$-th equation for $x_i$: $x^{(k+1)} = \frac{3 + y^{(k)}}{4}$, $y^{(k+1)} = \frac{3 + x^{(k)}}{4}$.

Step 3: Part b): Convergence
The matrix is **strictly diagonally dominant** ($4 > |{-1}|$ in each row), so the Jacobi method converges. Iteration matrix $B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & \tfrac14 \\ \tfrac14 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ with spectral radius $\rho(B) = \frac14 < 1$.

Step 4: Part b): Error evolution
The error $\vec e^{(k)} = \vec x^{(k)} - (1,1)$ is multiplied by $\frac14$ per step: $0.25 \to 0.0625 \to 0.0156$. Indeed $1 - 0.75 = 0.25$, $1 - 0.9375 = 0.0625$ ✓.

exercises.title: Quadratic interpolation
exercises.description: Determine the degree-two polynomial through $(-1,2), (0,1), (1,2)$ in Lagrange form, simplify it and explain why it is symmetric. Evaluate it at $x = 0.5$.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Interpolation polynomial
$p(x) = 2\cdot\frac{x(x-1)}{2} + 1\cdot(1 - x^2) + 2\cdot\frac{x(x+1)}{2} = x^2 - x + 1 - x^2 + x^2 + x = x^2 + 1$.

Step 3: Symmetry
The data are symmetric about the $y$-axis ($f(-1) = f(1)$), and the interpolating polynomial is unique; therefore it must be even: $p(x) = x^2 + 1$.

Step 4: Check and evaluation
$p(-1) = 2$ ✓, $p(0) = 1$ ✓, $p(1) = 2$ ✓. $p(0.5) = 1.25$. Note: between the nodes the function from which the data come may deviate; the interpolation error is $\frac{f'''(\xi)}{3!}(x+1)x(x-1)$.

exercises.title: Trapezoidal and Simpson rule for sin x
exercises.description: Approximate $\int_0^\pi\sin x\,dx = 2$ with $n = 4$ subintervals by the trapezoidal and Simpson rules and determine the errors.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Trapezoidal rule
$T = \frac h2\big(f_0 + 2f_1 + 2f_2 + 2f_3 + f_4\big) = \frac\pi8(2\cdot0.7071 + 2 + 2\cdot0.7071) = \frac\pi8\cdot4.8284 \approx 1.8961$. Error $\approx 0.104$.

Step 3: Simpson's rule
$S = \frac h3\big(f_0 + 4f_1 + 2f_2 + 4f_3 + f_4\big) = \frac\pi{12}(4\cdot0.7071 + 2 + 4\cdot0.7071) = \frac\pi{12}\cdot7.6569 \approx 2.0046$. Error $\approx 0.0046$.

Step 4: Interpretation
Simpson is here about $22$ times more accurate than the trapezoidal rule (error order $h^4$ vs. $h^2$). The trapezoidal rule underestimates because $\sin$ is concave on $[0,\pi]$ (the chords lie below the graph). Check: $\frac\pi8(2 + 2\sqrt2) \approx 1.896$ ✓.

exercises.title: Linear regression by least squares
exercises.description: Determine the best-fit line $y = a + bx$ through $(1,2), (2,2), (3,4), (4,5)$ and compute the sum of squared errors.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Coefficients
$b = \frac{5.5}{5} = 1.1$, $a = \bar y - b\bar x = 3.25 - 2.75 = 0.5$. Line: $y = 0.5 + 1.1x$.

Step 3: Residuals
Predictions $1.6;\ 2.7;\ 3.8;\ 4.9$. Residuals $0.4;\ -0.7;\ 0.2;\ 0.1$. Sum $0$ ✓.

Step 4: Sum of squared errors and check
$\sum r_i^2 = 0.16 + 0.49 + 0.04 + 0.01 = 0.70$. Orthogonality: $\sum x_ir_i = 0.4 - 1.4 + 0.6 + 0.4 = 0$ ✓. No other line has a smaller sum of squared errors (e.g. $y = x + 1$: residuals $0; -1; 0; 0$, sum of squares $1.0 > 0.70$).

exercises.title: Euler method and stability
exercises.description:
Consider $y' = -2y$, $y(0) = 1$ (exact $y = e^{-2x}$).
a) Compute two steps of the explicit Euler method with $h = 0.1$.
b) Compute two steps of the implicit Euler method and compare with $e^{-0.4}$.
c) For which $h$ is the explicit method stable?
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a): Explicit Euler method
$y_{n+1} = y_n + h(-2y_n) = (1 - 2h)y_n = 0.8y_n$. $y_1 = 0.8$, $y_2 = 0.64$.

Step 2: Part b): Implicit Euler method
$y_{n+1} = y_n + h(-2y_{n+1}) \Rightarrow y_{n+1} = \frac{y_n}{1 + 2h} = \frac{y_n}{1.2}$. $y_1 = 0.8333$, $y_2 = 0.6944$.

Step 3: Comparison with the exact solution
$e^{-0.4} = 0.6703$. Error: explicit $0.64 - 0.6703 = -0.030$, implicit $0.6944 - 0.6703 = +0.024$. Both methods have order $1$; the explicit one underestimates, the implicit one overestimates.

Step 4: Part c): Stability
For the explicit method $y_n = (1 - 2h)^ny_0$. The method is stable (solution decays) exactly for $|1 - 2h| < 1 \iff 0 < h < 1$. For $h = 1.2$: factor $-1.4$, the solution oscillates and grows — although the exact solution decays. The implicit method is stable for all $h > 0$: factor $\frac{1}{1 + 2h} \in (0,1)$.
